mekki-muskil:11-11.t: His saying {تأمنا}: its origin is تأمنُنا; then the first nūn was assimilated into the second, and the ishmām (lip-rounding) remained to indicate the ḍamma of the first nūn. Ishmām is rounding your lips without an audible sound; it comes after the assimilation and before the fatḥa of the second nūn. Ibn Kaysān calls ishmām "indication (ishāra)" and calls rawm "ishmām". Rawm is a weak sound heard faintly; it occurs in the nominative, the genitive, and the accusative that has no nunation, whereas ishmām occurs only in the nominative.

mekki-muskil:12-12.t: His saying {يرتع}: whoever of the readers gives kasra to the ʿayn takes it from رعى, dropping the yāʾ for the jussive; so it is yaftaʿil, and the tāʾ is augmentative, from the grazing (raʿy) of sheep. It has also been said it is from their saying رعاك الله, i.e. "may Allah guard you", so its meaning on this view is "we guard one another". Whoever reads it with sukūn on the ʿayn made it quiescent for the jussive and took it from رتع, so it is yafʿal and the tāʾ is a radical.

mekki-muskil:13-13.t: His saying {أَن تذْهبُوا بِهِ} and {أَن يَأْكُلهُ}: the first أن is in the position of nominative (marfūʿ) as the agent of يحزنني, and the second أن is in the position of accusative (manṣūb) as the object of أخاف.

mekki-muskil:16-16.t: His saying {عشَاء}: accusative as an adverb (ẓarf), and it is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the implied pronoun in جَاءُوا.

mekki-muskil:17-17.t: His saying {وَلَو كُنَّا}: al-Mubarrad said: لو means إن.

mekki-muskil:18-18.t:
His saying {بِدَم كذب}: i.e. "possessing falsehood (ذِي كذب)".
His saying {فَصَبر جميل}: nominative on the implication of a mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "my affair is a beautiful patience (فأمري صَبر جميل)" or "my state is a beautiful patience (فشأني صَبر جميل)". Quṭrub said its implied form is "my patience is a patience (فصبري صَبر)", with جميل as a naʿt (adjective) of الصبر. The accusative is permissible — though it was not read — as a maṣdar (verbal noun), on the implied form "I will be patient with patience (فَأَنا أَصْبِر صبرا)". The nominative is the preferred choice in it because it is not a command; had it been a command, the preferred choice in it would have been the accusative.

mekki-muskil:19-19.t:
His saying {يَا بشرى}: Ibn Abī Isḥāq and others read it with a doubled yāʾ without alif (يا بُشْرَيَّ). The reason for that is that the yāʾ of annexation requires what precedes it to have kasra; since that is not possible with the alif, it was turned into yāʾ and assimilated into the yāʾ of annexation; its like is هُدَيَّ. The Kufans read it without yāʾ, as though they made بشرى the name of the one addressed, so it is in the position of ḍamma. It has also been said that he addressed the good news itself, as though he said: "O good news, this is your time!" On this meaning the readers read يَا حسرة على الْعباد with nunation, as though he addressed the regret.
His saying {وأسروه}: the hāʾ is for Yūsuf, peace be upon him, and the pronoun [of the agent] is for his brothers; it has also been said the pronoun is for the merchants. بضاعة is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from Yūsuf, its meaning being "made into merchandise".

mekki-muskil:2-2.t: His saying, the Exalted, {قُرْآنًا عَرَبيا}: قُرْآنًا is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ in أَنزَلْنَاهُ, and its meaning is "We sent it down gathered together"; عربيا is another ḥāl. It is also permissible for قُرْآنًا to be a preparatory element (tawṭiʾa) for the ḥāl, with عربيا being the ḥāl, just as you say مَرَرْت بزيد رجلا صَالحا ("I passed by Zayd, a righteous man"): رجل is preparatory to the ḥāl and صالح is the ḥāl.

mekki-muskil:20-20.t: His saying {دَرَاهِم}: in the position of genitive as a badal (substitute) from ثمن.

mekki-muskil:23-23.t:
His saying {هيت لَك}: it is an indeclinable (mabnī) word without hamza, in which fatḥa, kasra and ḍamma on the tāʾ are all permissible; the kasra in it is far-fetched because of the heaviness of kasra after yāʾ. Its meaning is drawing Yūsuf to herself, in the sense of "come here (هَلُمَّ لَك)"; from it is their saying هيت فلَان بفلان when he calls him. As for whoever gives it hamza, he takes it from تهيأت لَك ("I have made myself ready for you"); there is some remoteness in this in meaning, because she was not informing him of her state, that she had made herself ready for him; she was only calling him to herself. As for whoever gives it hamza and ḍamma on the tāʾ, that is good, because he takes it from تهيأت لَك, making it a verb, treating it as her informing him of her state, with the tāʾ, which is the tāʾ of the speaker. Hamza with kasra on the tāʾ is far-fetched, because Yūsuf, peace be upon him, did not address her so that the tāʾ would be the address to her; rather it was she who called him and addressed him, so with hamza only ḍamma on the tāʾ is good. Had the address been from Yūsuf, he would have said هيت لي, reporting about himself, and that is not read. As for fatḥa and kasra on the hāʾ, they are two dialects. لَك in هيت لَك is for clarification (tabyīn), like سقيا لَك ("may you be watered").
His saying {معَاذ الله}: accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun); you say عاذ بِهِ معَاذًا, ومعاذة, وعياذا, وعياذة.
His saying {إِنَّه رَبِّي أحسن مثواي}: ربي is in the position of accusative as a badal (substitute) from the hāʾ, and أحسن is the khabar (predicate) of إن. If you wish, you may make the hāʾ refer to the matter (al-ḥadīth, i.e. a pronoun of the matter) as the noun of إن, with ربي in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject) and أحسن its khabar, and the clause in the position of the khabar of إن.
His saying {إِنَّه لَا يفلح}: the hāʾ refers to the matter and is the noun of إن, and what follows it is the khabar.

mekki-muskil:24-24.t:
His saying {لَوْلَا أَن رأى}: أن is in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is omitted.
The rule of لو is that it enters on verbs, because of the meaning of condition in it, yet verbs are not made jussive by it even though it contains the meaning of condition, because it does not change the meaning of the past into the future as the conditional particles do. Its meaning is the non-occurrence of a thing because of the non-occurrence of something else. If a noun occurs after it, it is nominative on the implication of a verb, except أنّ, after which what follows is nominative as mubtadaʾ, because the verb within its structure makes the implication of a verb before it unnecessary.
If you add لا to it, the meaning of condition leaves it, and after it comes the mubtadaʾ, with the khabar implied in most speech; it must have an answer, overt or implied; only nouns follow it, and its meaning becomes the non-occurrence of a thing because of the existence of something else. So the implied form of the verse is: "had he not seen the proof of his Lord at that time, such-and-such would have come from him"; thus the khabar and the answer are both omitted.
If لولا means هلا ("why not"), a verb comes after it, as in His saying فلولا كَانَت قَرْيَة, and this is frequent; its meaning in this case is urging (taḥḍīḍ) to something. You may imply the verb after it, saying لَوْلَا فعلت خيرا, or if you wish you may say لَوْلَا خيرا. Its counterpart in this meaning is لوما. This is how لو and لولا behave, so know it, for it is a difficult matter that recurs often.
His saying {كَذَلِك لنصرف}: the kāf is in the position of nominative on the implication of a mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "the matter of the proofs is like that (أَمر الْبَرَاهِين كَذَلِك)". It may also be in the position of accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar, its implied form being "We showed him the proofs with a showing like that (أريناه الْبَرَاهِين رُؤْيَة كَذَلِك)".

mekki-muskil:27-27.t: His saying {وَإِن كَانَ قَمِيصه}: إن is conditional, and it turns all past forms to the meaning of the future except كان, because of the strength of كان and the abundance of its use; that is because it is used to express all verbs.

mekki-muskil:31-31.t:
His saying {حاش لله}: the original form of حاش is with the alif, but it occurs in the codex without alif, the fatḥa sufficing for the alif, just as the nūn was dropped in لم يَك. حاشى is a past verb on the pattern fāʿala, taken from al-ḥashā, which is "the side", as al-Hudhalī said:
... بِأَيّ الحشا صَار الخليط المباين ...
(To which side has the departing companion gone?)
i.e. to which side the companion has gone. It is not good for it to be a particle according to the people of reasoning (ahl al-naẓar), though Sībawayh permitted that; the Kufans disallowed it, because if it were a preposition it would not enter on a preposition, and because nothing is dropped from particles except when they contain a doubling, as in لَعَلَّ and عَلّ. The meaning of حاش لله is the distance of Yūsuf from that of which he was accused, for Allah's sake, i.e. because of his fear of Allah and his mindfulness of Him.
Al-Mubarrad said حاشى can be a particle and can be a verb, and he argued that it can be a verb from the saying of al-Nābigha:
... وَلَا أحاشي من الأقوام من أحد ...
(And I do not except anyone among the peoples.)
So من أحد is in the position of accusative by أحاشي. Someone else said حاشى is a particle and أحاشي is a verb taken from the particle and built from its letters, just as they said لَا اله إِلَّا الله and then a verb was derived from the letters of this sentence: they said هلل الرجل; likewise their saying بسمل فلَان when he says بِسم الله, and حوقل when he says لَا حول وَلَا قُوَّة إِلَّا بِاللَّه; and this is frequent.
Al-Zajjāj said the meaning of حاش لله is "a declaration of innocence for Allah the Exalted", so its meaning is: Yūsuf has been kept apart from that of which he was accused. The lexicographers related حَشا لله, with the first alif dropped, and it is a dialect.
The accusative with حاشى in exception is better according to al-Mubarrad, because it is a verb in most of its states; Sībawayh holds the genitive with it, because it is a preposition.

mekki-muskil:4-4.t:
His saying {إِذْ قَالَ يُوسُف}: the governor of إِذْ is His saying الغافلين. Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif read يُؤسِف, with kasra on the sīn and with hamza, making it Arabic on the pattern yufʿil from al-asaf ("grief"), but it is a diptote because of definiteness and the verbal pattern. Abū Zayd related يُؤسَف, with fatḥa on the sīn and with hamza, making it yufʿal from al-asaf as well; so it is Arabic, and a diptote for the reason we mentioned. Whoever puts ḍamma on the sīn makes it a foreign word, a diptote because of definiteness and foreignness; there is no yufʿul [pattern] in the speech of the Arabs, and therefore it was not Arabic on this pattern.
His saying {يَا أَبَت}: the tāʾ in يَا أَبَت, when you give it kasra in continuous speech, is a substitute for the yāʾ of annexation (the first-person possessive) according to Sībawayh; in his view the tāʾ and the yāʾ of annexation are not combined, and in his view one does not pause on His saying يَا أَبَت except with hāʾ, since there is no implied yāʾ there. That is how Ibn Kathīr and Ibn ʿĀmir paused. Al-Farrāʾ said the yāʾ is intended, so one pauses on His saying يَا أَبَت with tāʾ; most of the readers paused that way, following the codex. Ibn ʿĀmir read it with fatḥa on the tāʾ: he assumed the tāʾ to be dropped in the manner of its dropping in tarkhīm (vocative truncation), then restored it without taking it into account, so he gave it fatḥa just as the noun had fatḥa before its return, as they say يَا طَلْحَة, يَا أُمَيْمَة with fatḥa. The analogy for pausing on this view is that you pause with hāʾ, as one pauses on طَلْحَة and أُمَيْمَة. It has also been said that he intended يَا أبتا and then dropped the alif because the fatḥa indicates it; on this view you must pause with tāʾ, because the alif is intended and implied. It has also been said that he intended يَا أبتاه and then dropped [the ending], but this is not a place of lamentation (nudba). Al-Naḥḥās permitted ḍamma on the tāʾ, likening it to the tāʾ of طَلْحَة when it is not truncated, and al-Zajjāj disallowed it.
His saying {ساجدين}: a ḥāl from the hāʾ and mīm in رَأَيْتهمْ, because it is from seeing with the eye. He reported about the stars with the yāʾ and nūn [plural], which are for rational beings, only because, when He reported about them obedience and prostration, which are acts of rational beings, ساجدين was treated as reporting about rational beings, since the act of rational beings had been related about them.

mekki-muskil:6-6.t: His saying {كَمَا أتمهَا}: the kāf is in the position of accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar, its implied form being "a completing like that with which He completed it (اتماما كَمَا أتمهَا)".

mekki-muskil:7-7.t:
His saying {آيَات للسائلين}: concerning the pattern of آيَة there are four views. Sībawayh said it is faʿla, its origin being أَيْيَة; then they replaced the quiescent yāʾ with an alif. This is the meaning of what he said, and its like in his view is غَايَة and ثاية. Its weakening (iʿlāl) is anomalous in his view, because they weakened the middle radical (ʿayn) and kept the final radical (lām) sound, whereas the analogy is weakening the lām and keeping the ʿayn sound.
The Kufans said آيَة is faʿala, with fatḥa on the ʿayn, its origin being أَيَيَة; the first yāʾ was turned into alif because it was vowelled and preceded by fatḥa. This is anomalous in weakening, since the rule was to weaken the second yāʾ and keep the first sound, so that one would say أياة.
Some of the Kufans said آيَة is faʿila, its origin being أَيِيَة; the first yāʾ was turned into alif because it had kasra and what preceded it was vowelled, and the first was more entitled to weakening than the second because of the heaviness of the kasra on it. This is a sound view that runs according to the principles.
Ibn al-Anbārī said آيَة is on the pattern fāʿila, its origin being آيِيَة; the first yāʾ was made quiescent out of finding the kasra on the yāʾ heavy, and they assimilated it into the second, so it became آيّة, like the form and pattern of دَابَّة; then they lightened the yāʾ, just as they said كينونة with the yāʾ lightened and quiescent, its origin being كيّنونة; then they lightened it by dropping the first, vowelled yāʾ, out of finding the doubled yāʾ heavy together with the length of the word. This is a view far from analogy, since there is no length in آيَة requiring the dropping, as there is in كينونة.

mekki-muskil:9-9.t:
His saying {أَرضًا يخل لكم}: أَرضًا is an adverb (ẓarf). Al-Naḥḥās mentioned that it is not indefinite in sense (mubham), and the verb's due was not to reach it except through a preposition, but the preposition was dropped, as the poet said:
... كَمَا عسل الطَّرِيق الثَّعْلَب ...
(As the fox trots [along] the road.)
There is room for consideration in what he said.

mekki-muskil:100-100.t: His saying {وخروا لَهُ سجدا}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the implied pronoun in خروا, and it is an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara).

mekki-muskil:107-107.t: His saying {بَغْتَة}: a ḥāl (circumstantial), and its origin is the maṣdar (verbal noun).

mekki-muskil:109-109.t: His saying {ولدار الْآخِرَة}: in this speech there is an omitted muḍāf; its implied form is "and the abode of the final state (ولدار الْحَال الْآخِرَة)". Al-Farrāʾ said this is the annexation of a thing to itself, because the abode is the Hereafter. It has also been said it is the annexation of the qualified noun to its attribute, because the abode was described as "the last (الآخرة)", as He said in another place وللدار الْآخِرَة, as an attribute.

mekki-muskil:111-111.t: His saying {وَلَكِن تَصْدِيق}: تصديق is accusative as the khabar (predicate) of an implied كان; its implied form is "but that was a confirmation (وَلَكِن كَانَ ذَلِك تَصْدِيق)". The nominative is permissible on the implied form "but it is a confirmation (وَلَكِن هُوَ تَصْدِيق)", but no one read it so.

mekki-muskil:35-35.t: His saying {ثمَّ بدا لَهُم}: the fāʿil (agent) of بدا, according to Sībawayh, is omitted, and ليسجننه stands in its place. Al-Mubarrad said its agent is the maṣdar (verbal noun) indicated by بدا. It has also been said that the agent is omitted with nothing substituted for it, its implied form being "then an opinion appeared to them (ثمَّ بدا لَهُم رأي)".

mekki-muskil:38-38.t: His saying {مَا كَانَ لنا أَن نشْرك بِاللَّه من شَيْء}: أن is the noun of كان and لنا is the khabar (predicate) of كان; من شَيْء is in the position of accusative as the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of نشرك, and من is redundant (zāʾida), emphasizing the negation.

mekki-muskil:40-40.t: His saying {سميتموها}: the basic rule of سمّى is that it takes two objects, one of which may be omitted; the second is omitted here, its implied form being "you named them gods (سميتموها آلِهَة)". أنتم is a tawkīd (emphasis) of the tāʾ in سميتموها, so that conjoining to it becomes good.

mekki-muskil:41-41.t: His saying {فيسقي ربه خمرًا}: سقى and أسقى are two dialects. It has also been said that سقى means "to hand someone water", and أسقى "to provide someone with drink"; from this is His saying, the Exalted, وأسقيناكم مَاء فراتا, i.e. We provided that for you.

mekki-muskil:43-43.t: His saying {سمان}: the genitive is as a naʿt (adjective) of البقرات, and likewise خضر is genitive as a naʿt of سنبلات. The accusative is permissible in سمان and in خضر as a naʿt of سبع, as He, the Exalted, said سبع سماوات طباقا, as a naʿt of سبع; and the genitive of طباق as a naʿt of سموات is permissible. But nothing is read except what has a sound transmission and agrees with the script of the codex.

mekki-muskil:47-47.t: His saying {دأبا}: accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), because the meaning of تزرعون indicates "you persevere (تدأبون)". Abū Ḥātim said: whoever gives fatḥa to the hamza in دأبا — and it is the reading of Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim — makes it the maṣdar of دئب, and whoever gives it sukūn makes it the maṣdar of دأبت. Fatḥa on the hamza in the verb is what is well known among the lexicographers, while fatḥa and sukūn in the maṣdar are two dialects, like their saying النَّهَر and النَّهْر, السَّمَع and السَّمْع. It has also been said that it was vowelled and made quiescent only because of the guttural letter.

mekki-muskil:64-64.t:
His saying {خير حَافِظًا}: حفظا is accusative as a specification (bayān, i.e. tamyīz), because they had attributed to themselves the guarding of Yūsuf's brother, saying وَإِنَّا لَهُ لحافظون; so Yaʿqūb answered them in that, and said: Allah the Exalted is better in guarding than your guarding.
As for whoever reads it حَافِظًا, he made it accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) according to al-Naḥḥās: a ḥāl from Allah, exalted be His mention, on the basis that Yaʿqūb returned their very word, since they had said وَإِنَّا لَهُ لحافظون, and he informed them that Allah is the Guardian, so the two expressions ran on a single course. Annexation (iḍāfa) is permissible in this reading: you say الله خير حَافظ ("Allah is the best of guardians"), as He said أرْحم الرَّاحِمِينَ. Annexation is not permissible in the first reading: you do not say الله خير حفظ, because Allah the Exalted is not the guarding; He, the Exalted, is the Guardian.
Some of the people of reasoning said that حَافِظًا is not accusative as a ḥāl, because afʿal (the elative) must have a specification; were it permissible to make it accusative as a ḥāl, it would be permissible to omit it, and were it omitted, the clarity of the speech would be deficient, and the expression would become "and Allah is better", so one would not know in what kind the "better" is. The permissibility of annexation indicates that it is not a ḥāl, and making it accusative as a specification is better, like the accusative of حفظ; this is the view of al-Zajjāj and others.

mekki-muskil:65-65.t: His saying {مَا نبغي}: مَا is in the position of accusative by نبغي, and it is interrogative. It may also be a negation, in which case pausing on نبغي is good; with the interrogative, pausing on نبغي is not good, because the clause after it is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial).

mekki-muskil:75-75.t:
His saying {قَالُوا جَزَاؤُهُ من وجد فِي رَحْله فَهُوَ جَزَاؤُهُ}: the first جزاؤه is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and the khabar (predicate) is omitted; its implied form is: Yūsuf's brothers said, "the recompense of the thief with us is like his recompense with you". It has also been said the implied form is "the recompense of theft with us is like its recompense with you"; so the hāʾ refers to the thief or to the theft. Then من is nominative as mubtadaʾ, and it means الذي (relative) or is conditional.
His saying {فَهُوَ جَزَاؤُهُ}: a mubtadaʾ and khabar in the position of the khabar of من; the fāʾ is the answer to the condition, or an answer because of the vagueness in الذي. The hāʾ in فهو refers to the "استبعاد" [Translator's note: the text has استبعاد ("distancing"); the context suggests استعباد ("enslavement"), but it is translated as written], and the hāʾ in the last جزائه refers to the thief or to the theft.
It has also been said that the first جزاؤه is a mubtadaʾ and من is its khabar on the assumption of an omitted muḍāf; its implied form is: Yūsuf's brothers said, "the recompense of theft is the استبعاد of whoever it is found in his saddlebag; so that is its recompense", i.e. the استبعاد is the recompense of theft; and in this view the hāʾs refer to the theft and nothing else.
It has also been said that the first جزاؤه is a mubtadaʾ and من is a second mubtadaʾ, being conditional or meaning الذي; فهو جزاؤه is the khabar of the second, and the second with its khabar is a khabar of the first; the second جزاؤه refers back to the first mubtadaʾ because it is put in the place of the pronoun, as though you said "so it is it (فَهُوَ هُوَ)".
His saying {استيأسوا}: this and ييأس are all from يئس ييأس. As for what al-Bazzī related from Ibn Kathīr, putting the yāʾ after the alif (استايسوا), it is by metathesis (qalb): he put the hamza before the yāʾ, so it became يأيس; then he lightened the hamza and replaced it with alif.
His saying {إِنَّه من يتق ويصبر}: من is conditional, nominative as mubtadaʾ, and فإن الله with what follows it is the khabar; the clause is the khabar of the first إنّ, and the hāʾ refers to the matter (al-ḥadīth). ويصير [Translator's note: so in the text; the verse has ويصبر] is conjoined to يتق.
As for what Qunbul related from Ibn Kathīr, that he read يتقي with yāʾ, its justification is that he made من mean الذي, so he put يتقي in the nominative because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of من, and conjoined ويصير [Translator's note: i.e. ويصبر] on the meaning of the speech: because من, even when it means الذي, contains the meaning of condition, and for that reason the fāʾ enters its khabar in most places. Since it contains the meaning of condition, he conjoined ويصبر on that meaning and put it in the jussive, just as Allah the Exalted said فَأَصدق وأكن: He put وأكن in the jussive, construing it on the meaning of فأصدق, because it is in the sense of أصدق in the jussive, since it is the answer to the wish (tamannī).
It has also been said that من in this reading is conditional and the ḍamma is implied on the yāʾ of يتقي, [the implied vowel] having been dropped for the jussive, as [the poet] said:
... ألم يَأْتِيك والأنباء تنمي ...
(Did it not reach you — and news spreads —)
There is weakness in this, because this kind of assumption is mostly permissible only in poetry. It has also been said that من means الذي and يصبر is nominative by conjunction to يتقي, but the ḍamma was dropped for lightness; this too is far-fetched. Al-Akhfash related that he heard from the Arabs رسْلنا with sukūn on the lām for lightness. Keeping the yāʾ in يتقي together with the jussive of يصبر is not strong, whichever way you interpret it.
His saying {كَذَلِك نجزي}: the kāf is in the position of accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "with a recompense like that We recompense the wrongdoers".

mekki-muskil:76-76.t:
His saying {إِلَّا أَن يَشَاء الله}: أن is in the position of accusative on the assumption of the dropping of the preposition, i.e. "except by Allah's willing (إِلَّا بِأَن يَشَاء الله)".
His saying {نرفع دَرَجَات من نشَاء}: the Kufans read it with nunation on درجات, so it [من] is in the position of accusative by نرفع, and the preposition with درجات is omitted; its implied form is "We raise whom We will to degrees (نرفع من نشَاء إِلَى دَرَجَات)". Whoever does not give nunation to درجات makes it accusative by نرفع and annexes it to من.

mekki-muskil:77-77.t:
His saying {فقد سرق}: سرق is a past verb that is reported speech (maḥkī); its implied form is "it has been said: a brother of his stole", since it is not permissible that they asserted theft against Yūsuf with certainty, for the prophets of Allah are too exalted for that; they only reported a matter that had been said, without asserting it.
His saying {مَكَانا}: accusative as a specification (bayān).

mekki-muskil:79-79.t: His saying {أَن نَأْخُذ}: أن is in the position of accusative on the assumption of the dropping of the preposition, i.e. "I seek refuge in Allah from our taking (أعوذ بِاللَّه معَاذًا من أَن نَأْخُذ)".

mekki-muskil:80-80.t:
His saying {نجيا}: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the implied pronoun in خلصوا; it is a singular that conveys the meaning of the plural.
His saying {وَمن قبل مَا فرطتم فِي يُوسُف}: مَا may be redundant (zāʾida), with من attached to (mutaʿalliq) فرطتم, its implied form being "and you fell short before regarding Yūsuf"; this is far-fetched because of the separation between the conjunction and what it is conjoined to. قبل is indeclinable (mabnī) because of the omission of what it is annexed to; its implied form is "and before this time you fell short regarding Yūsuf".
If you make مَا and the verb a maṣdar (verbal noun), من is not attached to فرطتم, because you would be putting the ṣila before the relative; rather it is attached to [an implied notion of] stability (istiqrār), because the maṣdar is nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject) and what precedes it is its khabar (predicate); there is room for consideration in this.
It is also permissible for من to be attached to تعلموا in His saying ألم تعلمُوا, so that مَا فرطتم is a maṣdar in the position of accusative by conjunction to أن, the governor being تعلموا; this is ugly because of the separation between the conjunction and the conjoined by من قبل. It is good according to the Kufans and ugly according to the Basrans.

mekki-muskil:92-92.t: His saying {لَا تَثْرِيب عَلَيْكُم الْيَوْم}: it is not permissible for the governor of اليوم to be لا تثريب, because then it would become part of its completion, while تثريب has been made indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, and it is not permissible to make a noun indeclinable before it is complete. Rather you make اليوم accusative as an adverb (ẓarf) and make it the khabar (predicate) of تثريب, and عليكم is an attribute of تثريب; على is attached to an implied [word] that is originally an attribute of تثريب, its implied form being "there is no reproach established upon you today (لَا تَثْرِيب ثَابت عَلَيْكُم الْيَوْم)", so you make اليوم accusative by the [notion of] stability (istiqrār). It is also permissible to make اليوم accusative by عليكم and to imply a khabar for تثريب, because عليكم and what it governs is an attribute of تثريب. It is also permissible to make عليكم the khabar of تثريب and to make اليوم accusative by عليكم; the governor of اليوم is originally the omitted [word] to which على is attached.

mekki-muskil:96-96.t: His saying {فَارْتَد بَصيرًا}: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).
